title: Caro-Kann Defense: the ideas
line: Like the French, but the side pawn leaves a bishop free to come out before the pawns close it in.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its king two squares, into the center.
Push the pawn on c7 one square. It gets ready to back up a pawn on d5.

also.e7e5: That is the open game, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Caro-Kann.
also.c7c5: That is the Sicilian Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Caro-Kann.

also.g8f6: That is the Alekhine Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Caro-Kann.

steps.text: Now push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It hits the pawn on e4, and your pawn on c6 guards it.
steps.after: White guards the pawn with a knight.

steps.text: Take the pawn on e4. White's knight takes back, and your bishop can then come out and hit it.
In the French a pawn shuts one bishop in. Here its way is open. Tap the bishop that can come out now.
steps.after: The pawn in front of your king is still at home, so this bishop's path is clear.

steps.text: Bring it out to f5, where it hits the knight on e4.

also.b8d7: That is the Karpov Variation, another main line. This lesson goes on with the bishop.
also.g8f6: That also works. This lesson goes on with the bishop.

steps.after: The knight steps away and hits the bishop back.

summary: The Caro-Kann builds a solid center like the French, but the bishop comes out before the pawns close it in.
